text:
Marta Ibarra: Hi team I opened PR #4218 to add a compact migration checklist and refresh SDK snippets for Optimize (batching, kv-prefetch, quant profiles). Need a quick sanity pass.

Kevin Liu: I can look. Which snippet variants are highest risk? Python streaming or the Go microbatch?

Marta Ibarra: Both. Python uses `batching_hint` + `kv_prefetch=true` in the example; Go might still reference the old `BatchConfig` type.

Julia Park: Skimmed the diff: link to prefetch design doc points to /deckhand/optkit-old (broken). Also a stray space after the Go code fence caused mkdocs to fail locally.

Samir Dutta: Quant profiles include a short-seq example for LLaMA-2-13B assuming int8. Recommend adding a short note: run a smoke eval (100 prompts) to check delta.

Marta Ibarra: Good call. I'll add the smoke-eval note and a pytest snippet. Also will fix the link and code fence.

Kevin Liu: One nit: showing SDK param names ties us to v0.9+. Maybe show the raw JSON request body instead and add a migration note linking to SDK migration guide.

Julia Park: Agreed. JSON is safer. Add an inline comment about SDK name changes and escape any inline backticks so mkdocs doesn't choke.

Samir Dutta: In Go sample replace `BatchConfig.MaxTokens` with `batch_options.max_tokens` and flip `EnableKVPrefetch` to the new `enable_kv_prefetch` boolean. I tested that locally against the mock.

docs-bot: deploy preview: https://deploy-preview.redwood/docs/4218 build: success, warnings: 1 link, 2 lint.

Marta Ibarra: Thanks all. I'll push fixes in ~20m and tag @Kevin @Julia for final review. Also adding a tiny docs/tests snippet that runs the Python example against a mock to avoid rot. :pray:
